objective: At the owner's request ('Yes continue.', approving FAR-READ-20261106-001's recommendation): prove that a Fano atom acts as one from outside, that is, every line of another Fano atom receives the same creation, far side by far side, whichever of the atom's lines is removed. Find the mechanism, prove what holds in every knot space, state exactly what remains open, and test the open part on fresh spaces. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-07: successful, with one finite exception left to computation. A Fano atom with a line removed is transparent: in every knot space it sends the free relation through each of its cuts (closed sides act as their lost elements; the plain Fano plane is the only signed Fano knot). Deep points of a removal's side never decide creation at a Fano atom's line and add far sides only at receiving cut lines with a six-pattern relation; free passes through closed atoms. So a Fano atom acts as one: for creation in every knot space, far side by far side outside that place and fully on Fano trees; on 277 computed spaces every Fano atom line receives exactly its closed verdict (154,165 pairs), the exception included. Next: the genus reading on Fano trees (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when acts-as-one is proved in every knot space, or reduced to an explicitly stated finite exception that is tested on fresh spaces fixed in advance, or refuted by a counterexample.
title: Why a Fano atom acts as one
